title: What-if runway scenario cookbook
purpose: One-page experimental workbook to model 'what-if' runway scenarios for mid-phase launches. Combines a compact KPI tracker, 3 stress scenarios, and a minimal phase-gate checklist so product ops can surface risks and mitigations quickly for launch reviews.
executive_summary: This workbook tests three realistic traffic/cost/quality permutations and shows near-term key signal thresholds that should block or proceed for a scaled rollout. Intended for rapid iteration with engineering and SRE before formalizing into the release playbook.
assumptions: Baseline traffic: 25k daily requests routed to hosted API (avg payload 800 tokens)
Dedicated pool available at +15% throughput cost increase for guaranteed capacity
Latency SLO target: p95 <= 450ms for user-facing generation endpoints
Cost model uses 0.002 USD per generation token (hosted) and 0.0012 USD/token on dedicated after quantization
Fallback model reduces quality (BLEU-style proxy) by ~12% but keeps latency < 300ms
runway_inputs: Availability of dedicated nodes: yes/no toggle
Reserve buffer: 20% headroom for sudden spikes
Retention of prefix cache: expected 40% reuse for conversational traffic
scenario_definitions: Scenario A: Fast adoption + noisy input distribution — traffic doubles in 10 days, 30% queries are long-context (>1024 tokens). Stress on memory/kv-cache and request queueing.
Scenario B: Steady growth + cost pressure — linear growth, token mix stable, but finance requests cost cap at month end; need cost-control knobs (quantization, batching changes).
Scenario C: Spike & degradation — external event generates 5x traffic for 48 hours; fallback strategy, model routing, and rate-limiting must maintain p99 < 2s and error rate < 1%
kpi_rows: User growth | 25k DAU | 30k | 60k | Priya Desai | Pause onboarding / enable throttles
p95 latency | 380ms | 450ms | 950ms | Noah Kim | Enable low-latency routing / fallback model
Error rate | 0.4% | 0.5% | 3.2% | Liam Chen | Rollback recent model config / open SEV
Cost / 1k tokens | $1.90 | $2.00 | $3.70 | Finance (Ava Martinez) | Enable quantization profile B / cap traffic
Cache hit rate | 42% | 40% | 18% | Serving runtime team | Increase prefix caching TTL / warm cache
phase_gate_checklist: Gate 0 (pre-alpha): E2E smoke tests passing locally, basic telemetry (latency, errors, cost) enabled
Gate 1 (alpha): Canary to 1% traffic, no P0 issues in 72h, identified owner for each top-5 KPI
Gate 2 (beta): Ops runbook completed, rollback playbook dry-run, SLOs validated with synthetic traffic
Gate 3 (ramp): Autoscaling policy stress-tested, dedicated pool fallback configured, billing alert thresholds set
Gate 4 (full): Stakeholder sign-off, documentation for customer support, incident response on-call assigned
contingency_playbook: If p95 > 600ms: switch routing to low-cost low-latency model variant for up to 30% of requests; notify growth for throttling
If cost projection > budget cap: incrementally enable quantization levels and enable per-route token limits; notify finance and PAUSE non-critical experiments
If error rate above 1% sustained 30m: automatic rollback to previous stable model and page SRE
If cache-hit drops below 25%: run cache-warm job on top N prefixes and extend cache TTL by +50% for 2h
If traffic spike > 3x: engage surge squad, temporarily restrict throughput for anonymous users and prioritize paid traffic
simulation_notes: Micro-sim script (local) takes inputs: starting DAU, growth rate, token distribution, dedicated-toggle. Use these knobs to produce daily P50/P95, cost burn, and hit-rate. This doc stores manual runs — export results to /analytics/launch-sims for formal analysis.
